name: Example: Solving for a Coefficient in a 2x2 Linear System Using Cramer's Rule
problem:
Let $\langle x,3 \rangle$ be the solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}5x-2y=4 \\ x+ky=8\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following equations could be solved to find the value of $k?$

- ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14057622/assets/b82f5c43c9ec788b95e7213bef63eb37e4abf9d0159f92cbeedc0f64c4d35283.png)

- ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14057622/assets/648ce0c1b8b77c1230c6c634c676624f9c79c12ffc3942abc09d24d0fdc424d3.png)

- ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14057622/assets/bc7a566778813050611b098cebe221aa77ac27677e922cd282fc8ff9c3670cfd.png)
worked_solution:
The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 1 & k\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $y$ is given by $y=\dfrac{D_y}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 4 \\ 1 & 8\end{aligned}| \\  & =5\cdot 8-4\cdot 1 \\  & =36.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D} \\ 3 & =\frac{36}{|\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 1 & k\end{aligned}|} \\ |\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 1 & k\end{aligned}| & =12\end{aligned}
$$

So, the correct answer is "II only".
